findings.title: Consumer SAC inspection retains cancelled registrations and crashes after channel close
findings.requirement: Consumer.consuming_from_sac(queue) must report whether the Consumer is consuming from a SAC queue; Consumer.is_active_on(queue) and active_consumer_tags must reflect actual active ownership across the requested cancellation and channel-close lifecycle.
findings.evidence: Reproduced with a real memory transport in /tmp/kombu-consumer-review-repro.py. Create a Consumer on a SAC Queue, consume, then call channel.basic_cancel(tag). channel.consumer_info(queue) becomes [], but consumer.consuming_from_sac(queue) still returns True. _on_cancel only invokes user callbacks and never reconciles _active_tags, while consuming_from_sac trusts that stale mapping. Calling consumer.consume() again also leaves the registry empty because _basic_consume sees the stale tag. In a separate run, channel.close() cancels the registration, but each of consuming_from_sac(queue), is_active_on(queue), and active_consumer_tags raises AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'state', because these helpers access broker state through the closed channel. Repair the new inspection methods to verify actual current registration and handle a closed channel, and reconcile true cancellations without treating SAC demotion (which uses the same notification callback) as deregistration. Add coverage for direct Channel.basic_cancel and Channel.close, not only Consumer.cancel.

findings.title: Active Consumer queries confuse identical tags on different channels
findings.requirement: Consumer.is_active_on(queue) and Consumer.active_consumer_tags must identify this Consumer's active registration; broker-wide consumer state must correctly distinguish registrations across channels.
findings.evidence: Reproduced with a real memory transport in /tmp/kombu-consumer-review-repro.py. Start a Consumer on channel A on a SAC queue; obtain its generated tag. Register a higher-priority consumer on channel B with that same tag using basic_consume. consumer_info correctly shows channel B's registration active and channel A's registration inactive, and publishing delivers only to B. However, channel A's Consumer.is_active_on(queue) returns True and active_consumer_tags includes the demoted tag. The helper compares only the tag string returned by get_active_consumer, discarding registration/channel identity. Duplicate tags across channels are explicitly supported by the added test test_duplicate_tags_on_different_channels_have_one_active_record. Repair the Consumer helpers to check both channel ownership and active registration (for example, channel-local consumer records), and add a Consumer-level duplicate-tag test verifying inactive status after demotion and active status after failover.

findings.title: Selected SQS consumers inherit another registration's acknowledgement mode
findings.requirement: Priority/SAC delivery in the virtual transport layer must dispatch to the correct consumer, while preserving the existing Queue.consume(no_ack=False) manual-acknowledgement contract. Standby registrations must not change how the active consumer's messages are acknowledged.
findings.evidence: Reproduced using the actual SQS Channel conversion, bulk receive, virtual dispatcher, and acknowledgement methods, substituting only the external AWS client. Declare SAC queue jobs; register priority-0 low with no_ack=True, then priority-10 high with no_ack=False. Fetch one valid Kombu payload through low._get_bulk('jobs'). Delivery correctly selects high, but the backend delete_message has already been called once BEFORE high acknowledges. The delivered message also lacks sqs_message/sqs_queue metadata; acknowledging it performs no additional backend deletion. SQS._message_to_python checks the queue-level _noack_queues and deletes/returns the payload before the new dispatcher chooses the receiving registration. Thus a no-ack standby makes the active manual-ack consumer's delivery unrecoverable if processing fails. Reproduction script: /tmp/review_consumer_repro.py. Existing documentation explicitly assigns acknowledgement responsibility to the user for manual acknowledgements (docs/userguide/consumers.rst:46-47).
findings.recommended_change: Integrate consumer selection with SQS acknowledgement handling: retain receipt metadata until dispatch and apply the selected registration's no_ack mode rather than a queue-level flag contributed by another consumer. Cover mixed-ack registrations on SAC and non-SAC queues, including a full active consumer and standby fetches. Do not treat this backend dependency as unrelated to the requested virtual-layer delivery semantics.

findings.title: SAC consumption query remains true after transport-side cancellation
findings.requirement: Consumer.consuming_from_sac(queue) must return True only when this Consumer is consuming from a SAC queue, including correct lifecycle state after Channel.basic_cancel.
findings.evidence: Reproduced on memory:// without mocking: create Consumer(channel, [Queue('sac-query', queue_arguments={'x-single-active-consumer': True})]); call consume(); obtain its registered tag and call channel.basic_cancel(tag). channel.get_consumer_count('sac-query') is then 0, but consumer.consuming_from_sac('sac-query') returns True. The method relies on consuming_from(), which only checks the Consumer's cached _active_tags. Transport-side cancellation invokes _on_cancel, but that method only calls notification callbacks and never reconciles the cache. The new helper therefore contradicts the authoritative BrokerState registration immediately after the requested cancellation operation. Reproduction script: /tmp/review_consumer_repro.py.
findings.recommended_change: Make the new query consult live registrations owned by this Consumer's channel/tag, or otherwise reconcile definitive cancellation with Consumer bookkeeping. Preserve cached registration/standby state on SAC demotion, since demotion also invokes on_cancel but does not remove the registration. Add a test that distinguishes definitive cancellation from demotion.
